5.s_dismas: The cup which you haue ſtollen, is that wherin my lord doth drinke, and wherin he is wont to diuine: you haue done a verie euil thing.

5.sabates_a: The cup which you have stolen is that wherein my lord doth drink, and wherein he is wont to divine: you have done a very evil thing.
5.madueke_b: The cup which you have stolen is that wherein my lord doth drink, and wherein he is wont to divine: you have done a very evil thing.

6.s_dismas: He did as he had commanded. And hauing ouertaken them, he ſpake to them in the ſame order.
6.odr_com: He did as he had commanded. And hauing ouertaken them, he spake to them in the same order.
6.sabates_a: He did as he had commanded. And having overtaken them, he spake to them in the same order.
6.madueke_b: He did as he had commanded. And having overtaken them, he spake to them in the same order.

7.s_dismas: Who anſwered: Why doth our lord ſpeake ſo, as though thy ſeruantes had committed ſo haynous a fact?
7.odr_com: Who answered: Why doth our lord speake so, as though thy seruautes had committed so haynous a fact?
7.sabates_a: Who answered: Why doth our lord speak so, as though thy servants had committed so heinous a fact?
7.madueke_b: Who answered: Why doth our lord speak so, as though thy servants had committed so heinous a fact?

8.s_dismas: The money, that we found in the top of our ſackes, we recaried to thee from the land of Chanaan: and how foloweth it, that we haue ſtollen out of thy lordes houſe, gold or ſiluer?
8.odr_com: The money, that we found in the top of our sackes, we recaried to thee from the land of Chanaan: and how foloweth it, that we haue stollen out of thy lordes house, gold or siluer?
8.sabates_a: The money that we found in the top of our sacks, we recarried to thee from the land of Chanaan: & how followeth it, that we have stolen out of thy lord's house gold or silver?
8.madueke_b: The money that we found in the top of our sacks, we recarried to thee from the land of Chanaan: & how followeth it, that we have stolen out of thy lord's house gold or silver?

9.s_dismas: With whom ſoeuer of thy ſeruantes that shal be found, which thou ſeekeſt, let him die, and we wil be the bondmen of our lord.
9.odr_com: With whom soeuer of thy seruantes that shal be found, which thou seekest, let him die, and we wil be the bondmen of our lord.
9.sabates_a: With whom soever of thy servants that shall be found which thou seekest, let him die, and we will be the bondmen of our lord.
9.madueke_b: With whom soever of thy servants that shall be found which thou seekest, let him die, and we will be the bondmen of our lord.

10.s_dismas: Who ſaid to them: Be it done according to your ſentence: with whom ſoeuer it shal be found, be he my bondman, and you shal be guiltles.
10.odr_com: Who said to them: Be it done according to your sentence: with whom soeuer it shal be found, be he my bondman, and you shal be guiltles.
10.sabates_a: Who said to them: Be it done according to your sentence: with whom soever it shall be found, be he my bondman, and you shall be guiltless.
10.madueke_b: Who said to them: Be it done according to your sentence: with whom soever it shall be found, be he my bondman, and you shall be guiltless.

11.s_dismas: Therfore in haſte taking downe their ſackes vpon the ground, euerie man opened.
11.odr_com: Therfore in haste taking downe their sackes vpon the ground, euerie man opened.
11.sabates_a: Therefore in haste taking down their sacks upon the ground, every man opened.
11.madueke_b: Therefore in haste taking down their sacks upon the ground, every man opened.

12.s_dismas: Which when he had ſearched, beginning from the elder euen to the youngeſt, he found the cup in Beniamins ſack.
12.odr_com: Which when he had searched, beginning from the elder euen to the youngest, he found the cup in Beniamins sack.
12.sabates_a: Which when he had searched, beginning from the elder even to the youngest, he found the cup in Benjamin's sack.
12.madueke_b: Which when he had searched, beginning from the elder even to the youngest, he found the cup in Benjamin's sack.

13.s_dismas: But they renting their garments, and loading their aſſes againe, returned into the towne.
13.odr_com: But they renting their garments, and loading their asses againe, returned into the towne.
13.sabates_a: But they renting their garments, and loading their asses again, returned into the town.
13.madueke_b: But they renting their garments, and loading their asses again, returned into the town.

14.s_dismas: And Iudas foremoſt with his brethren entred in to Ioſeph (for he was not yet gone out of the place) and they fel togeather before him on the ground.
14.odr_com: And Iudas foremost with his brethren entred in to Ioseph (for he was not yet gone out of the place) and they fel togeather before him on the ground.
14.sabates_a: And Judas foremost with his brethren entered in to Joseph (for he was not yet gone out of the place) and they fell together before him on the ground.
14.madueke_b: And Judas foremost with his brethren entered in to Joseph (for he was not yet gone out of the place) and they fell together before him on the ground.

15.s_dismas: To whom he ſaid: Why would you doe ſoe? know you not that there is not the like to me in the ſcience of diuining.
15.odr_com: To whom he said: Why would you doe soe? know you not that there is not the like to me in the science of diuining.
15.sabates_a: To whom he said: Why would you do so? Know you not that there is not the like to me in the science of divining.
15.madueke_b: To whom he said: Why would you do so? Know you not that there is not the like to me in the science of divining.

16.s_dismas: To whom Iudas ſaid: What shal we anſwere, my lord? or what shal we ſpeake, or be able iuſtly to pretend? God hath found the iniquitie of thy ſeruantes: loe we are al bondmen to my lord, both we, & he, with whom the cup was found.
16.odr_com: To whom Iudas said: What shal we answere, my lord? or what shal we speake, or be able iustly to pretend? God hath found the iniquitie of thy seruantes: loe we are al bondmen to my lord, both we, & he, with whom the cup was found.
16.sabates_a: To whom Judas said: What shall we answer, my lord? Or what shall we speak, or be able justly to pretend? God hath found the iniquity of thy servants: lo we are all bondmen to my Lord, both we, & he with whom the cup was found.
16.madueke_b: To whom Judas said: What shall we answer, my lord? Or what shall we speak, or be able justly to pretend? God hath found the iniquity of thy servants: lo we are all bondmen to my Lord, both we, & he with whom the cup was found.

17.s_dismas: Ioſeph anſwered: God forbid that I should ſo doe: he that ſtole the cup, the ſame be my bondman: and goe you free vnto your father.
17.odr_com: Ioseph answered: God forbid that I should so doe: he that stole the cup, the same be my bondman: and goe you free vnto your father.
17.sabates_a: Joseph answered: God forbid that I should so do: he that stole the cup, the same be my bondman: and go you free unto your father.
17.madueke_b: Joseph answered: God forbid that I should so do: he that stole the cup, the same be my bondman: and go you free unto your father.

18.s_dismas: And Iudas approching nearer, ſaid boldly: I beſeech thee my lord, let thy ſeruant ſpeake a word in thine eares, and be not angrie with thy ſeruant: for after Pharao thou art,
18.odr_com: And Iudas approching nearer, said boldly: I beseech thee my lord, let thy seruant speake a word in thine eares, and be not angrie with thy seruant: for after Pharao thou art,
18.sabates_a: And Judas approaching nearer said boldly: I beseech thee my lord, let thy servant speak a word in thine ears, and be not angry with thy servant: for after Pharao thou art,
18.madueke_b: And Judas approaching nearer said boldly: I beseech thee my lord, let thy servant speak a word in thine ears, and be not angry with thy servant: for after Pharao thou art,

19.s_dismas: my lord. Thou dideſt aske thy ſeruantes the firſt time: Haue you a father or a brother?
19.odr_com: my lord. Thou didest aske thy seruantes the first time: Haue you a father or a brother?
19.sabates_a: my Lord. Thou didst ask thy servants the first time: Have you a father or a brother?
19.madueke_b: my Lord. Thou didst ask thy servants the first time: Have you a father or a brother?

20.s_dismas: and we anſwered thee my lord: We haue a father an old man, and a little boy, that was borne in his old age; whoſe brother by the mother is dead: and his mother hath him only, and his father loueth him tenderly.
20.odr_com: and we answered thee my lord: We haue a father an old man, and a little boy, that was borne in his old age; whose brother by the mother is dead: and his mother hath him only, and his father loueth him tenderly.
20.sabates_a: and we answered thee my lord: We have a father an old man, and a little boy, that was born in his old age; whose brother by the mother is dead: and his mother hath him only, and his father loveth him tenderly.
20.madueke_b: and we answered thee my lord: We have a father an old man, and a little boy, that was born in his old age; whose brother by the mother is dead: and his mother hath him only, and his father loveth him tenderly.

21.s_dismas: And thou ſaidſt to thy ſeruants: Bring him hither to me, and I wil ſet myn eyes on him.
21.odr_com: And thou saidst to thy seruants: Bring him hither to me, and I wil set myn eyes on him.
21.sabates_a: And thou saidst to thy servants: Bring him hither to me, and I will set mine eyes on him.
21.madueke_b: And thou saidst to thy servants: Bring him hither to me, and I will set mine eyes on him.

22.s_dismas: We ſuggeſted to my lord: The boy can not leaue his father: for if he leaue him, he wil die.
22.odr_com: We suggested to my lord: The boy can not leaue his father: for if he leaue him, he wil die.
22.sabates_a: We suggested to my lord: The boy cannot leave his father: for if he leave him, he will die.
22.madueke_b: We suggested to my lord: The boy cannot leave his father: for if he leave him, he will die.

23.s_dismas: And thou ſaideſt to thy ſeruants: Vnleſſe your youngeſt brother come with you, you shal no more ſee my face.
23.odr_com: And thou saidest to thy seruants: Vnlesse your youngest brother come with you, you shal no more see my face.
23.sabates_a: And thou saidst to thy servants: Unless your youngest brother come with you, you shall no more see my face.
23.madueke_b: And thou saidst to thy servants: Unless your youngest brother come with you, you shall no more see my face.

24.s_dismas: Therfore when we were gone vp to thy ſeruant our father, we told him al things that my lord did ſpeake.
24.odr_com: Therfore when we were gone vp to thy seruant our father, we told him al things that my lord did speake.
24.sabates_a: Therefore when we were gone up to thy servant our father, we told him all things that my lord did speak.
24.madueke_b: Therefore when we were gone up to thy servant our father, we told him all things that my lord did speak.

25.s_dismas: And our father ſaid: Goe againe, and bye vs a litle wheate.
25.odr_com: And our father said: Goe againe, and bye vs a litle wheate.
25.sabates_a: And our father said: Go again, and buy us a little wheat.
25.madueke_b: And our father said: Go again, and buy us a little wheat.

26.s_dismas: To whom we ſaid: We can not goe: if our youngeſt brother shal goe downe with vs, we wil ſet forward together: otherwiſe he being abſent, we dare not ſee the mans face.
26.odr_com: To whom we said: We can not goe: if our youngest brother shal goe downe with vs, we wil set forward together: otherwise he being absent, we dare not see the mans face.
26.sabates_a: To whom we said: We cannot go: if our youngest brother shall go down with us, we will set forward together: otherwise he being absent, we dare not see the man's face.
26.madueke_b: To whom we said: We cannot go: if our youngest brother shall go down with us, we will set forward together: otherwise he being absent, we dare not see the man's face.

27.s_dismas: Wherunto he anſwered: You know that my wife bare me two.
27.odr_com: Wherunto he answered: You know that my wife bare me two.
27.sabates_a: Whereunto he answered: You know that my wife bare me two.
27.madueke_b: Whereunto he answered: You know that my wife bare me two.

28.s_dismas: One went forth, and you ſaid: A beaſt did deuour him: and hitherto he appeareth not.
28.odr_com: One went forth, and you said: A beast did deuour him: and hitherto he appeareth not.
28.sabates_a: One went forth, and you said: A beast did devour him: and hitherto he appeareth not.
28.madueke_b: One went forth, and you said: A beast did devour him: and hitherto he appeareth not.

29.s_dismas: If you take this alſo, and ought befal him in the way, you shal bring downe my hoare hayres with ſorow vnto hel.
29.odr_com: If you take this also, and ought befal him in the way, you shal bring downe my hoare hayres with sorow vnto hel.
29.sabates_a: If you take this also, and ought befall him in the way, you shall bring down my hoar hairs with sorrow unto hell.
29.madueke_b: If you take this also, and ought befall him in the way, you shall bring down my hoar hairs with sorrow unto hell.

30.s_dismas: Therfore if I shal enter to thy ſeruant our father, and the boy be wanting (wheras his life dependeth vpon the life of him)
30.odr_com: Therfore if I shal enter to thy seruant our father, and the boy be wanting (wheras his life dependeth vpon the life of him)
30.sabates_a: Therefore if I shall enter to thy servant our father, and the boy be wanting (whereas his life dependeth upon the life of him)
30.madueke_b: Therefore if I shall enter to thy servant our father, and the boy be wanting (whereas his life dependeth upon the life of him)

31.s_dismas: and he shal ſee that he is not with vs, he wil dye, & thy ſeruants shal bring downe his hoare hayres with ſorow vnto hel.
31.odr_com: and he shal see that he is not with vs, he wil dye, & thy seruants shal bring downe his hoare hayres with sorow vnto hel.
31.sabates_a: and he shall see that he is not with us, he will die, and thy servants shall bring down his hoar hairs with sorrow unto hell.
31.madueke_b: and he shall see that he is not with us, he will die, and thy servants shall bring down his hoar hairs with sorrow unto hell.

32.s_dismas: Let me be thy proper ſeruant, that did take him into my protection and promiſed ſaying: Vnleſſe I bring him againe I wil be guilty of ſinne againſt my father for euer.
32.odr_com: Let me be thy proper seruant, that did take him into my protection and promised saying: Vnlesse I bring him againe I wil be guilty of sinne against my father for euer.
32.sabates_a: Let me be thy proper servant that did take him into my protection and promised, saying: Unless I bring him again I will be guilty of sin against my father for ever.
32.madueke_b: Let me be thy proper servant that did take him into my protection and promised, saying: Unless I bring him again I will be guilty of sin against my father for ever.

33.s_dismas: I therfore thy ſeruant wil tary in ſteed of the childe in the ſeruice of my lord, and let the childe goe vp with his brethren.
33.odr_com: I therfore thy seruant wil tary in steed of the childe in the seruice of my lord, and let the childe goe vp with his brethren.
33.sabates_a: Itherefore thy servant will tarry instead of the child in the service of my lord, and let the child go up with his brethren.
33.madueke_b: I therefore thy servant will tarry instead of the child in the service of my lord, and let the child go up with his brethren.

34.s_dismas: For I can not returne to my father, the childe being abſent; leſt I ſtand by a witnes of the calamitie, that ſhal oppreſſe my father.
34.odr_com: For I can not returne to my father, the childe being absent; lest I stand by a witnes of the calamitie, that shal oppresse my father.
34.sabates_a: For I cannot return to my father, the child being absent; lest I stand by a witness of the calamity that shall oppress my father.
34.madueke_b: For I cannot return to my father, the child being absent; lest I stand by a witness of the calamity that shall oppress my father.

janvier_by_verse.1: And Joseph commanded the steward of his house, saying: Fill their sacks with corn, as much as they can hold: and put the money of every one in the top of his sack.
janvier_by_verse.2: And in the sack's mouth of the younger put my silver cup, and the price which he gave for the wheat. And it was so done.
janvier_by_verse.3: And when the morning rose, they were dismissed with their asses.
janvier_by_verse.4: And they were now departed out of the city, and had gone forward a little way: then Joseph sending for the steward of his house, said: Arise, quote he, and pursue the men: and overtaking them say to them: Why have you rendered evil for good?
janvier_by_verse.5: The cup which you have stolen is that wherein my lord doth drink, and wherein he is wont to divine: you have done a very evil thing.
janvier_by_verse.6: He did as he had commanded. And having overtaken them, he spake to them in the same order.
janvier_by_verse.7: Who answered: Why doth our lord speak so, as though thy servants had committed so heinous a fact?
janvier_by_verse.8: The money that we found in the top of our sacks, we recarried to thee from the land of Chanaan: & how followeth it, that we have stolen out of thy lord's house gold or silver?
janvier_by_verse.9: With whom soever of thy servants that shall be found which thou seekest, let him die, and we will be the bondmen of our lord.
janvier_by_verse.10: Who said to them: Be it done according to your sentence: with whom soever it shall be found, be he my bondman, and you shall be guiltless.
janvier_by_verse.11: Therefore in haste taking down their sacks upon the ground, every man opened.
janvier_by_verse.12: Which when he had searched, beginning from the elder even to the youngest, he found the cup in Benjamin's sack.
janvier_by_verse.13: But they renting their garments, and loading their asses again, returned into the town.
janvier_by_verse.14: And Judas foremost with his brethren entered in to Joseph (for he was not yet gone out of the place) and they fell together before him on the ground.
janvier_by_verse.15: To whom he said: Why would you do so? Know you not that there is not the like to me in the science of divining.
janvier_by_verse.16: To whom Judas said: What shall we answer, my lord? Or what shall we speak, or be able justly to pretend? God hath found the iniquity of thy servants: lo we are all bondmen to my Lord, both we, & he with whom the cup was found.
janvier_by_verse.17: Joseph answered: God forbid that I should so do: he that stole the cup, the same be my bondman: and go you free unto your father.
janvier_by_verse.18: And Judas approaching nearer said boldly: I beseech thee my lord, let thy servant speak a word in thine ears, and be not angry with thy servant: for after Pharao thou art,
janvier_by_verse.19: my Lord. Thou didst ask thy servants the first time: Have you a father or a brother?

janvier_by_verse.22: We suggested to my lord: The boy cannot leave his father: for if he leave him, he will die.
